clue.text: A variety of clay pit that's non-standard

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual clay pit, unlike the ordinary sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges the letters of CLAY PIT into TYPICAL, which follows the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something atypical departs from the usual pattern, so it is irregular or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Small amount from ditch?

definitions.meaning: a tiny quantity of liquid, as in a few spots of milk
to abandon or discard, as when a team leaves out a player

explanation.surface: A trickle of water taken from a drainage channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' looks like a noun, a trench, but it is the verb meaning to get rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday: a tiny spot of liquid, and to discard or abandon something.

clue.text: Singular vehicle making a mark

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: One particular vehicle leaves a mark, perhaps on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the lasting mark left on skin or a surface by a wound or damage.

clue.text: Chap taking exercise is big baboon

parts.note: a chap is a man
a drill is a training exercise, as in fire drill

explanation.surface: A man doing his workout turns out to be a huge ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrill is a large West African monkey closely related to baboons, famous for its colourful face.

clue.text: Reg and Sadie unfortunately don't see eye to eye

indicators.note: suggests things going wrong, so the letters of the two names are jumbled

explanation.surface: A couple called Reg and Sadie sadly have differences of opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the letters of REG and SADIE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who don't see eye to eye hold differing views; the idiom means to be in dispute.

clue.text: One half-dollar is an object of veneration

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word is its first three letters, taken here from dollar

explanation.surface: A single fifty-cent coin is revered like a holy relic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-dollar' looks like a coin, but 'half' takes the first three letters of DOLLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a figure or image that is worshipped, hence anything revered.

clue.text: Profit doubled repeatedly

definitions.meaning: two profits, read as one gain and a second gain

explanation.surface: Earnings multiplied by two, over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: a profit is a gain, so doubling it gives one gain and another gain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means many times over; the split phrase literally describes two profits.

clue.text: Karenin's wife going backwards or forwards

definitions.note: Tolstoy's heroine, married to Alexei Karenin, whose name is a palindrome

indicators.note: the name reads identically whichever direction you take it

parts.note: Tolstoy's heroine, married to Alexei Karenin, whose name is a palindrome

explanation.surface: Karenin's wife moving to and fro, a nod to her restless story.
explanation.walkthrough: Karenin is the husband in Tolstoy's novel Anna Karenina.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy's heroine is married to the official Alexei Karenin, so she is identified by her husband.

clue.text: Emergency treatment making tree respectable

parts.note: a fir is a conifer tree
staid means sober and respectable

explanation.surface: Urgent care that turns a tree into something respectable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immediate medical help given at the scene before professional care arrives.

clue.text: Unassailable prisoner outside a prison

indicators.note: the prisoner is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: An inmate standing outside the jail walls seems untouchable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is old slang for prison and 'con' for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast-iron argument or alibi is so solid that it cannot be challenged or broken.

clue.text: Drink produced from honey and nuts, packed with energy

indicators.note: something packed with an item holds it inside

parts.note: nuts means crazy, mad
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A drink brewed from honey and nuts, loaded with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic drink made by fermenting honey with water.

clue.text: Backward sketch?

parts.note: split as back and ward, the clue word reads as an instruction to turn a hospital room back to front; that the turned letters sit in the word is no coincidence but the rebus itself

explanation.surface: A rough drawing done the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Backward' into 'back' and 'ward': a ward taken back, read in reverse, is the answer. The word looks like a description of the sketch, but it is an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To sketch is to make a quick rough picture with pencil or pen, a synonym in verb form.

clue.text: Joke about English passenger ship

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on birds
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A gag about a British cruise ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A short quip delivered in a single sentence is a kind of joke.

clue.text: Adding nothing new after changing course

indicators.note: the nothing-new pieces come after the course change

parts.note: a sailing boat tacking is changing course against the wind
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sailor changing course adds nothing fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacking something on means appending it as an extra, so the phrasal verb fits the gerund.

clue.text: Recreation area — and area for coat

parts.note: a park is a public area for recreation

explanation.surface: A recreation ground, and a space set aside for coats.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket, originally worn in Arctic regions.

clue.text: Cold region in Italy — or northern county

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
Umbria is a region of central Italy

explanation.surface: A chilly part of Italy, or a county in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbria is a county in north-west England containing the Lake District.

clue.text: Weapon sometimes placed in front of corporal?

definitions.meaning: a long spear carried by mounted knights

definitions.text: sometimes placed in front of corporal?
definitions.meaning: the lowest rank of non-commissioned officer in the British Army is a ... corporal

explanation.surface: A spear sometimes carried ahead of a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A lance corporal is the junior rank just below corporal in the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a spear-like cavalry weapon and also the word preceding corporal in a military rank.

clue.text: Head of lettuce swallowed by bold sweetheart

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside what swallows it

parts.note: daring means bold

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here from lettuce

explanation.surface: A daring lover gulps down a lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' could mean a whole lettuce; here it takes L, which goes inside DARING.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling is a beloved person, a term of endearment for a loved one.

clue.text: Bird of prey originally observed without light

indicators.note: the original letters of the three words are their first ones

explanation.surface: A hunting bird first spotted in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The owl is a nocturnal raptor, hunting small animals at night.

clue.text: Changing into gear, I start

indicators.note: changing the letters means rearranging them into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver shifting into gear before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' sounds like a gear change but rearranges INTO GEAR I.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or arise, as an idea or a river starts somewhere.

clue.text: Where beef and dumplings may be beside oneself?

definitions.text: Where beef and dumplings may be
definitions.meaning: cooked slowly together in a casserole

explanation.surface: A cook's question about the whereabouts of the beef and dumplings.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the meat sits in a casserole; idiomatically the phrase means flustered and anxious.

clue.text: Disorder when grenade goes off

indicators.note: an exploding grenade scatters its pieces, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chaos follows when a grenade explodes.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw something into confusion or upset its normal arrangement.

clue.text: Give up on account of square on Monopoly board

parts.note: for means because of, as in famous for his wit
GO is the corner square where players start and collect money

explanation.surface: Quitting a board game because of landing on a square.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo is to do without or relinquish something willingly.

clue.text: Musical speeds in First Empire

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words First Empire, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: Music played fast or slow in Napoleon's First Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the Italian plural of tempo, the pace at which music is played.

clue.text: Duo not starting song

indicators.note: the word loses its starting letter

parts.note: a duo is a pair

explanation.surface: A duet that fails to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody, a simple song.
